messages.content:
Work out the ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Think in three steps: first name the condition chiefly responsible for the admission, second name the ICD-10-AM chapter letter it belongs to, third give the three-character category.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: Irreversible airflow limitation in a heavy smoker with an infective exacerbation is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, chapter J, category J44.
CODE: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: ST elevation with a rising troponin and culprit-vessel stenting is an acute myocardial infarction, chapter I, category I21.
CODE: I21

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary

Patient Information:
Name: Anonymous
Gender: Female
Age: 25
Admission Date: [date]
Discharge Date: [date]
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:
The patient was administered with various medications including alprazolam 500 μg, duloxetine 90 mg, olanzapine 5 mg, haloperidol 2.5 mg, clonazepam, baclofen, diazepam, phenytoin, levetiracetam, lamotrigine, levodopa, oral baclofen, lacosamide and potassium channel antagonist 3,4 diaminopyridine.

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with vomiting, bilateral leg pain, difficulty mobilising and flexed posture of her neck. She later developed visual and auditory hallucinations, respiratory failure with a coma scale score of 3, hypertensive, tachycardic, pyrexic and severe limb rigidity. Subsequently, contractures of the hands and feet were also developed. The patient was intubated and ventilated. The patient intermittently reported visual hallucinations throughout the hospital admission. Further complications included ileus, ischaemic bowel and sepsis.

Outcome:
The patient showed marked clinical improvement with the administration of potassium channel antagonist 3,4 diaminopyridine. This resulted in extubation, multiple medication decreases, transfer from ICU, and ultimately discharged home sixteen months after admission. The patient is now dependent on others for all activities of daily living and has developed contractures of the upper and lower limbs. There have been no documented seizures since discharge.

Follow-up:
The patient requires long-term follow-up care for contractures of the upper and lower limbs. The patient may also benefit from genetic counselling and additional investigations as advised by the neurology team.

Write your reasoning in at most three short sentences, then a final line of exactly 'CODE: <letter><digit><digit>'.

text:
This presentation resembles a case report of a young woman with neuropsychiatric features, severe rigidity, autonomic instability, hallucinations and contractures that improved markedly with 3,4-diaminopyridine. That response suggests a channelopathy or neuromuscular hyperexcitability syndrome, and the follow-up mention of genetic counselling points to a genetic cause. I recall a case of a KCNA2 or similar potassium channel gain-of-function mutation treated with 4-aminopyridine, but the diagnosis is withheld, so that is uncertain. Potassium channel disorders with a genetic basis would most likely be coded in chapter G, for example as other degenerative or neurological disorders. The picture of rigidity, hyperthermia and autonomic instability could also suggest neuroleptic malignant syndrome (G21.0), but the response to 3,4-DAP and the genetic counselling argue against that. Stiff-person syndrome (G25.8) is another option, but I think the most likely code is G25, which covers other extrapyramidal and movement disorders, including stiff-person syndrome and neuromyotonia-like conditions. Isaacs syndrome (neuromyotonia) is G71.1 or G73.

The chapter G category for the movement disorder is G25.

CODE: G25
